chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Hasan, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever a single day passes for him, and he prays in it five prayers, and does not recite in them 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' (Say, He is Allah, One), it will be said to him: 'O servant of Allah, you are not from the praying ones.'

key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say, He is Allah, One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas in daily prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to underscore the high status of Surah Al-Ikhlas as the 'essence' of the Quran, often equated with one-third of it in Shia tradition. The phrase 'not among the praying ones' is interpreted by scholars not as invalidating the prayer entirely, but as indicating a deficiency in spiritual perfection or completeness, urging believers to prioritize this concise declaration of divine unity in their daily worship.
